commands.description: The engine's name and version. Use it to confirm the engine is reachable before other calls.
commands.label: Engine Info
commands.name: system_info

commands.description: What this engine build offers: command count and groups, the length units, the project file format, the history limits and whether it runs as WebAssembly.
commands.label: Capabilities
commands.name: system_capabilities

commands.description: Discard the current garment and history and start an empty project in millimetres. Unsaved work is lost.
commands.label: New Project
commands.name: file_new

commands.description: Write the garment to a .ffbrc project file (a zip with manifest.json and garment.json). Entries of an opened project this engine does not know are kept.
commands.label: Save Project
commands.name: file_save

commands.description: Replace the current garment with the one in a .ffbrc project file and clear the history. Unsaved work is lost.
commands.label: Open Project
commands.name: file_open

commands.description: List the sample garments: a basic T-shirt, an A-line skirt with waistband and a sleeveless dress. Each is drafted from the body measurements.
commands.label: Samples
commands.name: sample_list

commands.description: Replace the garment with a sample drafted on the given or current body: the pattern panels are drawn from the body measurements, sewn, and placed around the body, ready for sim.reset and sim.run. Keeps the body and discards the previous garment and the whole undo history (the result says history_cleared). Fails with the code unsaved_changes when the open project has edits, unless force is true.

body.description: Body id in the project, or the name of a library body to load (MPFB2 Female or MPFB2 Male). Defaults to the first body, or MPFB2 Female when the project has none.

force.description: Replace a project that has unsaved edits. Without it the call fails with the code unsaved_changes so the caller can ask the user to confirm.

name.description: Sample garment, as listed by sample.list.

commands.label: Open Sample
commands.name: sample_load

commands.description: Undo the last step of the pattern history (a grouped drag counts as one step). Fails with nothing_to_undo when the history is at its start.
commands.label: Undo
commands.name: history_undo

commands.description: Redo the step last undone. Fails with nothing_to_redo when there is none; a new edit after an undo drops the redo steps.
commands.label: Redo
commands.name: history_redo

commands.description: Every history step with its label and whether it is applied, the current position, the step limit and whether undo and redo are available.
commands.label: History
commands.name: history_list

commands.description: Get or set the display length unit (mm, cm or in). Geometry is always stored in millimetres; only the unit shown and typed changes. Setting it is an undo step.

units.description: Length unit to switch to. Leave out to read the current unit.

commands.label: Units
commands.name: view_units

commands.description: Return the garment document: units, every panel with outline points, handles, inner shapes and placement, and the selection. Pass panel to return only that panel.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

commands.label: Pattern
commands.name: pattern_get

commands.description: Hit-test without changing the document. With at, return the panels under the position (top layer first) and the points and segments within tolerance, nearest first. With box, return panels fully inside (or touched when touch is true) and the points and segments inside the rectangle.

box.description: World rectangle [x0, y0, x1, y1] to select inside.

tolerance.description: Pick distance for points and segments under at.

touch.description: With box, also select panels the box only touches.

commands.label: Select
commands.name: pattern_select

commands.description: Measure a panel: segment lengths and chords, perimeter, area, orientation, centroid, bounds, self-intersections and the same for each inner shape. Without panel it reports every panel. All values are in mm and mm squared.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

commands.label: Measure
commands.name: pattern_measure

commands.description: Find where a world position snaps to: an outline point, a segment midpoint, an inner shape, the nearest spot on a segment, or the grid, within a tolerance in mm. Does not change the document. Returns the snapped position and the kind of target.

exclude.description: Panel ids to ignore, such as the panel being dragged.

grid.description: Grid spacing. 0 turns the grid target off.

targets.description: Snap targets to try, in priority order point, midpoint, inner, segment, grid. Defaults to all. inner covers inner shape points, midpoints and lines.

tolerance.description: Largest distance a target may be from the point.

commands.label: Snap
commands.name: pattern_snap

commands.description: Create a pattern panel from outline points given in world mm. Points may carry curve kinds and Bezier handles. The outline is stored counter-clockwise, placed at its lower left corner, and rejected when it has no area or crosses itself. Returns the new panel id.

name.description: Panel name. Defaults to Panel and the new id.

particle_distance.description: Simulation particle spacing for this panel.

points.description: Outline vertices in world mm, at least 3, in drawing order. A point is [x, y] or an object with p, kind, h_in and h_out. The outline is stored counter-clockwise.

h_in.description: Incoming handle as an offset from the point.

h_out.description: Outgoing handle as an offset from the point.

kind.description: corner: sharp vertex. curve: handles are computed from the neighbours. smooth: handles are kept collinear.

commands.label: Draw Panel
commands.name: pattern_draw_panel

commands.description: Create a rectangular panel from its lower left corner, width and height in mm, with an optional corner radius. Returns the new panel id.

corner_radius.description: Round all four corners by this tangent length; 0 keeps them sharp. Limited to half of the shorter side.

name.description: Panel name. Defaults to Panel and the new id.

particle_distance.description: Simulation particle spacing for this panel.

commands.label: Rectangle
commands.name: pattern_rectangle

commands.description: Create an elliptical panel from its centre and radii in mm as 4 or more smooth curve points with exact Bezier handles. Equal radii make a circle. Returns the new panel id.

name.description: Panel name. Defaults to Panel and the new id.

particle_distance.description: Simulation particle spacing for this panel.

ry.description: Radius along y. Equal to rx gives a circle.

segments.description: Number of curve points around the ellipse. 4 already gives a close fit.

commands.label: Ellipse
commands.name: pattern_ellipse

commands.description: Add an inner line, polyline, polygon, rectangle or ellipse to a panel. The shape must lie inside the outline. Rectangles take rect, ellipses take ellipse, the others take points. Optional fold angle and strength apply to open inner lines.

closed.description: Close a polyline into a loop. Polygons, rectangles and ellipses are always closed.

ry.description: Radius along y. Equal to rx gives a circle.

segments.description: Number of curve points around the ellipse. 4 already gives a close fit.

fold_angle.description: Fold angle of the inner line: 180 is flat, lower folds to the front, higher to the back.

fold_strength.description: How firmly the fold holds its angle, 0 for none.

kind.description: Shape to add. rectangle uses rect, ellipse uses ellipse, the others use points.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

points.description: Vertices: exactly 2 for line, at least 2 for polyline, at least 3 for polygon.

h_in.description: Incoming handle as an offset from the point.

h_out.description: Outgoing handle as an offset from the point.

kind.description: corner: sharp vertex. curve: handles are computed from the neighbours. smooth: handles are kept collinear.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

commands.label: Inner Shape
commands.name: pattern_inner_shape

commands.description: Add an open inner line through two or more points inside a panel, for folds, darts guides or sewing references. Returns the inner shape id.

fold_angle.description: Fold angle of the inner line: 180 is flat, lower folds to the front, higher to the back.

fold_strength.description: How firmly the fold holds its angle, 0 for none.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

points.description: Vertices of the inner line, at least 2. Two points make a line, more make a polyline.

h_in.description: Incoming handle as an offset from the point.

h_out.description: Outgoing handle as an offset from the point.

kind.description: corner: sharp vertex. curve: handles are computed from the neighbours. smooth: handles are kept collinear.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

commands.label: Inner Line
commands.name: pattern_inner_line

commands.description: Move one outline or inner-shape point to a position (to) or move one or several points by an offset (delta). Handles travel with the point and curve-kind neighbours re-flow. Use pattern.begin_drag and pattern.end_drag around many calls to make one undo step.

delta.description: Offset to add to every selected point.

indices.description: Several points to move together by delta; counts from 0.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

to.description: New position of the single point.

commands.label: Move Point
commands.name: pattern_move_point

commands.description: Set or remove the in or out Bezier handle of a point as an offset vector. On smooth points the opposite handle keeps its length and turns to stay collinear; with independent it does not.

independent.description: Break tangent continuity so the opposite handle stays put and the point becomes a corner.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

vector.description: Handle as an offset from the point. Leave out to remove the handle.

which.description: in: handle toward the previous point. out: handle toward the next point.

commands.label: Edit Handle
commands.name: pattern_set_handle

commands.description: Insert a point on a segment at curve parameter t or at the spot nearest to a position. The shape does not change; a curved segment is split into two exact curves. Returns the new point index.

at.description: Place the point at the spot on the segment nearest to this position.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

segment.description: Segment to add the point on; segment i runs from point i to point i+1. Optional with at.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

t.description: Curve parameter between 0 and 1 on the segment.

commands.label: Add Point
commands.name: pattern_add_point

commands.description: Split a segment by curve parameter t, by distance from its start in mm, or into equal pieces by count. Returns the indices of the new points.

count.description: Split into this many pieces of equal length.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

length.description: Split at this distance along the segment from its start.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

segment.description: Segment to split; segment i runs from point i to point i+1.

t.description: Split at this curve parameter between 0 and 1. The default is 0.5.

commands.label: Split Line
commands.name: pattern_split_line

commands.description: Remove a point; its two segments merge into one. An outline keeps at least 3 points, an open inner line at least 2.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

commands.label: Delete Point
commands.name: pattern_delete_point

commands.description: Convert a point to corner (sharp, no handles), curve (automatic handles that follow the neighbours) or smooth (editable collinear handles).

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

kind.description: corner: sharp, handles removed. curve: handles follow the neighbours automatically. smooth: keeps its handles collinear.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

commands.label: Point Kind
commands.name: pattern_set_point_kind

commands.description: Bend a segment into a symmetric curve by the bulge of its middle in mm; 0 straightens it. Positive bulges to the right of the segment direction.

amount.description: How far the middle of the segment bulges from the straight chord. Positive bulges to the right of the segment direction, which is outward on a counter-clockwise outline. 0 straightens the segment.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

segment.description: Segment to bend; segment i runs from point i to point i+1.

commands.label: Curvature
commands.name: pattern_curvature

commands.description: Round corner points with a Bezier arc that starts the given length from each corner along both edges. Returns how many corners were rounded and how many skipped.

curvature.description: 1 is a circular arc, 0 a straight bevel, above 1 a fuller corner.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

length.description: Distance from the corner where the rounding starts along each edge. Limited to half of the shorter neighbouring edge.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

points.description: Corner points to round, counted from 0. Corners next to curved segments are skipped.

commands.label: Smooth Corners
commands.name: pattern_smooth

commands.description: Mirror, scale, rotate and move whole panels in this order about a pivot (default: the centre of the selection). Rotation and translation change the panel placement; uneven scale and mirror rewrite the outline and keep it counter-clockwise. One undo step for all panels.

mirror.description: x flips left to right across the vertical line through the pivot, y flips top to bottom across the horizontal line.

panels.description: Panel ids to transform together.

pivot.description: Pivot for rotate, scale and mirror. Defaults to the centre of the selected panels.

scale.description: Scale factor about the pivot: one number for uniform scaling or [sx, sy] along the pattern axes. Uneven scaling bakes the panel rotation into its outline.

commands.label: Transform
commands.name: pattern_transform

commands.description: Copy panels with their inner shapes under new ids, shifted by offset per copy. Returns the created panel ids.

count.description: Number of copies of each panel.

offset.description: Shift between one copy and the next, starting from the original. Defaults to [20, 20].

panels.description: Panel ids to copy.

commands.label: Duplicate
commands.name: pattern_duplicate

commands.description: Remove panels and their inner shapes. Undo restores them at the same positions in the list.

panels.description: Panel ids to remove, with their inner shapes.

commands.label: Delete Panels
commands.name: pattern_delete

commands.description: Give a panel a new name of 1 to 64 characters.

name.description: New panel name.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

commands.label: Rename Panel
commands.name: pattern_rename

commands.description: Set particle distance, layer, grain direction, position or rotation on one or more panels, and the fold angle (0 to 360, 180 flat) and strength (0 to 20) of one inner line. Only the given values change.

fold_angle.description: Fold angle of the inner line: 180 is flat, lower folds to the front, higher to the back.

fold_strength.description: How firmly the fold holds its angle, 0 for none.

grain.description: Grain line direction inside the panel.

inner.description: Inner line id whose fold is set by fold_angle and fold_strength; needs exactly one panel.

layer.description: Layer order for overlapping panels; higher lies on top.

panels.description: Panel ids to change.

position.description: Absolute panel position on the pattern plane.

pressure.description: Inflation pressure of the panel in the solver's units, along the panel normal; 0 is none.

commands.label: Panel Properties
commands.name: pattern_set_props

commands.description: Open an undo group so many edits, such as repeated pattern.move_point calls during a mouse drag, become one history step. Close it with pattern.end_drag; undo and redo also close it.

label.description: Name of the undo step the drag becomes. Defaults to Drag.

commands.label: Begin Drag
commands.name: pattern_begin_drag

commands.description: Close the open undo group and commit its edits as a single history step. Safe to call when no group is open.
commands.label: End Drag
commands.name: pattern_end_drag

commands.description: Give panels a seam allowance stored on the panel: a general width in mm, a corner style (miter, square, round, mirror) and optional widths for single outline segments. clear removes it. The allowance outline is derived from the panel outline and follows later edits; the reply carries the derived outline, its length and area. Notches stay on the sewing outline.

clear.description: Remove the seam allowance from the panels.

corners.description: How a corner of the offset line is finished where the outline turns away from the offset. miter: the offset edges meet in a sharp point, cut back to a square corner beyond the miter limit. square: each edge is extended by the offset distance and cut square. round: a circular arc around the corner. mirror: a chamfer cut across the corner at the offset distance from it, as for a folded mitred corner.

panels.description: Panels to give or change the seam allowance of.

per_segment.description: Allowance width per outline segment, counted from segment 0; null uses the general width, and a shorter list leaves the rest on the general width. Needs exactly one panel.

width.description: Allowance width on every segment without its own override. A new allowance starts at 10 mm.

commands.label: Seam Allowance
commands.name: pattern_seam_allowance

commands.description: Offset a panel outline by a distance in mm (positive outward, negative inward), with Bezier segments refitted as cubic curves, per-segment distances, corner styles miter, square, round or mirror, and loops from inward offsets removed. Creates closed inner lines (inward only) or new panels laid over the source. Count makes several offsets in one step.

as.description: inner: closed inner lines inside the panel, which needs a negative distance. panel: new panels with the offset outline, placed over the source.

corners.description: How a corner of the offset line is finished where the outline turns away from the offset. miter: the offset edges meet in a sharp point, cut back to a square corner beyond the miter limit. square: each edge is extended by the offset distance and cut square. round: a circular arc around the corner. mirror: a chamfer cut across the corner at the offset distance from it, as for a folded mitred corner.

count.description: Number of offsets, each one distance further than the last.

distance.description: Offset distance. Positive grows the outline outward, negative retracts it inward.

miter_limit.description: Longest miter, as a multiple of the distance from the corner; beyond it a miter corner is cut square.

name.description: Name of the new panel. Defaults to the source name and offset.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

per_segment.description: Offset distance per outline segment, counted from segment 0, with the same sign as distance; null uses distance. Segments the list does not reach use distance.

commands.label: Offset Outline
commands.name: pattern_offset_outline

commands.description: Add a notch to the panel outline at curve parameter t of a segment, at a distance along a segment (length), or at the spot nearest a position (at). Kinds slit, v, t and u with depth, width and angle. Notches are stored by segment and t, so they keep their place when points are added, segments split or the panel moves. Returns the notch id, its local and world position and its outward normal.

angle.description: Angle between the notch and the outline tangent; 90 is square to the edge.

at.description: Place the notch at the spot on the outline nearest to this position.

depth.description: How far the notch reaches from the outline.

kind.description: slit: a short cut into the allowance. v: a V-shaped wedge. t: a T-shaped cut. u: a U-shaped cut.

length.description: Distance from the start of the segment along the curve.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

segment.description: Outline segment the notch sits on; segment i runs from point i to point i+1. Optional with at.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

t.description: Curve parameter between 0 and 1 along the segment.

width.description: Width of the notch across its opening; ignored by slits.

commands.label: Add Notch
commands.name: pattern_notch_add

commands.description: Change a notch: move it with segment and t, length or at, or change its kind, depth, width and angle. Only the given values change.

angle.description: Angle between the notch and the outline tangent; 90 is square to the edge.

at.description: Place the notch at the spot on the outline nearest to this position.

depth.description: How far the notch reaches from the outline.

kind.description: slit: a short cut into the allowance. v: a V-shaped wedge. t: a T-shaped cut. u: a U-shaped cut.

length.description: Distance from the start of the segment along the curve.

notch.description: Notch id as listed in the panel's notches.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

segment.description: Outline segment the notch sits on; segment i runs from point i to point i+1. Optional with at.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

t.description: Curve parameter between 0 and 1 along the segment.

width.description: Width of the notch across its opening; ignored by slits.

commands.label: Edit Notch
commands.name: pattern_notch_set

commands.description: Remove one notch by id, several by notches, or every notch of the panel with all.

all.description: Remove every notch of the panel.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

commands.label: Delete Notch
commands.name: pattern_notch_delete

commands.description: Set the grain line arrow of a panel from two points (from, to) or from an angle (centred on the panel, with an optional length), or clear it. Without a stored line the panel shows a default: vertical through the panel centre, half the panel height long; pattern.get reports it as grain_line_effective with computed true. Does not change the panel grain angle unless sync_grain is set.

angle.description: Direction of the line, counter-clockwise from the pattern x axis; 90 is vertical. The line is centred on the panel unless center is given.

center.description: Centre of a line made from angle. Defaults to the panel centre.

clear.description: Remove the stored line so the default, vertical through the panel centre, applies again.

length.description: Length of a line made from angle. Defaults to half the panel height, at least 20 mm.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

sync_grain.description: Also set the panel's grain angle to the line direction.

to.description: End of the grain line; the arrow points here.

commands.label: Grain Line
commands.name: pattern_grain_line

commands.description: Set the role (shape, fold, dart, reference), fold angle (0 to 360, 180 flat, lower folds to the front, higher to the back), fold strength (0 to 20) and closed state of an inner shape. Only the given values change; geometry is untouched.

closed.description: Whether the shape closes back on its first point.

fold_angle.description: Fold angle of the inner line: 180 is flat, lower folds to the front, higher to the back.

fold_strength.description: How firmly the fold holds its angle, 0 for none.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

role.description: shape: ordinary inner line. fold: the line folds at fold_angle. dart: a dart. reference: a construction line that does not shape the cloth.

commands.label: Inner Shape Properties
commands.name: pattern_set_inner

commands.description: List the length of every segment of a panel outline or inner shape in mm, with chord, end points, running total and the notches on each segment at their distance along it. With segments, also return the sum of those segments. Without panel it lists every panel outline. Does not change the document.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

segments.description: Only these segments count toward selected_total; the list still shows every segment.

commands.label: Segment Lengths
commands.name: pattern_segment_lengths

commands.description: Make a run of consecutive segments as long as the sum of reference segments (of this or another panel) or a given length, plus an optional ease. move_end slides the end point of the run along its chord; scale scales the run about its first point. Returns the lengths before and after.

ease.description: Added to the wanted length; negative shortens, as for easing a sleeve cap into an armhole.

how.description: move_end: slide the end point of the run along its chord until the run has the wanted length, the shape of the points before it unchanged. scale: scale the run about its first point, keeping its shape.

inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

length.description: Wanted length instead of a reference.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

reference_inner.description: Inner shape id inside the panel. Leave out to edit the panel outline.

reference_panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

reference_segments.description: Segments of the reference whose lengths add up to the wanted length. The reference panel defaults to the target panel.

segments.description: Consecutive segments of the target to resize together. For an outline the run may wrap past the last segment.

commands.label: Match Length
commands.name: pattern_match_length

commands.description: Cut a dart into a panel outline: the opening is width mm wide, centred at t on a segment, and its two equal legs meet at an apex length mm along the inward normal (or at a given apex point). The outline stays closed and valid or the command fails with invalid_geometry. With internal true it adds a closed triangular inner shape with role dart instead. Linked copies of the panel follow. Fails with linked_panel on a mirror copy or instance.

angle.description: Internal dart only: direction of the apex from the base centre, used with center and length.

apex.description: Apex point instead of a length.

center.description: Internal dart only: base centre, used instead of segment and t.

inset.description: Internal dart only: distance the base is moved inside the outline from the segment point.

internal.description: Create a closed inner dart shape with role dart instead of cutting the outline.

length.description: Dart length from the middle of the opening to the apex, along the inward normal. Give length or apex.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

segment.description: Outline segment that carries the dart opening. Segment i runs from point i to point i+1. For an internal dart it only locates the base.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

t.description: Position of the dart centre along the segment, 0 at its start and 1 at its end.

width.description: Dart opening (intake) measured along the segment, centred on t. For an internal dart the width of its base.

commands.label: Dart
commands.name: pattern_dart

commands.description: Cut a panel along a line from edge to edge and rotate the part on one side about the hinge end, by a spread distance at the free end or by an angle. The outline stays closed; the opened end is joined by a curve that continues the neighbouring tangents. Inner shapes and the grain line move with their part. Fails with invalid_geometry when the result would cross itself or an inner shape crosses the cut.

angle.description: Rotation of the moving part in degrees instead of a distance. Positive opens the cut.

from.description: First point of the cut line. The line runs through from and to and is used between the outline crossings nearest to them.

hinge.description: Which end of the cut stays joined. The part rotates about it.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

side.description: Which part moves, seen from the hinge looking along the cut: left, right, or both by half the spread each.

smooth.description: Join the opened end with a curve that continues the neighbouring outline tangents. false uses a straight edge.

space.description: world: coordinates on the pattern plane the user sees. local: coordinates inside the panel before its position, rotation and mirror apply.

spread.description: Opening of the cut at its free end, measured as a straight distance. Give spread or angle. Negative closes the cut.

to.description: Second point of the cut line.

commands.label: Slash and Spread
commands.name: pattern_slash_spread

commands.description: Mirror a half panel across one of its straight outline segments into one symmetric outline; the segment disappears. Inner shapes, notches and seam allowance values are mirrored too (inner shapes lying on the axis are not doubled).

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

segment.description: Straight outline segment to unfold about, usually the centre front or centre back. It disappears; the half is mirrored across it.

commands.label: Unfold
commands.name: pattern_unfold

commands.description: Create a panel shaped as a flat spiral strip of a given width that winds from the inner radius to the outer radius over a number of turns. Fails with invalid_geometry when neighbouring turns would overlap.

center.description: Centre of the spiral on the pattern plane.

inner_radius.description: Radius of the strip centre line where the spiral starts.

name.description: Panel name. Defaults to Spiral and the new id.

outer_radius.description: Radius of the strip centre line where the spiral ends.

particle_distance.description: Simulation particle spacing for this panel.

start_angle.description: Angle of the start of the strip.

turns.description: Number of turns from start to end.

commands.label: Spiral
commands.name: pattern_spiral

commands.description: Create a new panel from a closed inner shape (by inner id, or the smallest one containing the point at) or from a closed region given as vertices. The new panel keeps the traced geometry at the same place on the pattern plane. remove true also deletes the inner shape from the source panel.

at.description: World point: traces the smallest closed inner shape of the panel that contains it.

inner.description: Closed inner shape id to trace into a new panel.

name.description: Panel name. Defaults to Traced and the new id.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

particle_distance.description: Simulation particle spacing for the new panel. Defaults to the source panel's.

points.description: A closed region given by its vertices in world mm, in any winding. The panel is then optional and only supplies fabric, layer and grain.

remove.description: Remove the traced inner shape from the source panel.

commands.label: Trace
commands.name: pattern_trace

commands.description: Create a linked mirror copy of a panel across an axis (two points, or a straight outline segment such as the centre front), optionally set apart by a gap. The copy is derived: after every change to the source it is regenerated, inside the same undo step. Geometry edits made directly on the copy are discarded; pattern.dart, pattern.slash_spread, pattern.unfold and pattern.mirror_link fail with linked_panel on it. Name, fabric, layer, particle distance and 3D placement of the copy stay editable. Use pattern.unlink to make it independent.

axis.description: Mirror axis as two points [[x, y], [x, y]] in world mm. Give axis or axis_segment.

axis_segment.description: Use the straight line through this outline segment of the panel as the axis (for example the centre front).

gap.description: Extra distance between the panel and its mirror image across the axis.

name.description: Name of the mirror copy. Defaults to the source name and mirror.

panel.description: Panel id as listed by pattern.get.

interval.description: Shift between one copy and the next, in world mm. Defaults to the panel width plus 20 mm along x, or to the interval already in use.

name.description: Base name of new copies. Defaults to the source name and the copy number.

commands.description: Read a DXF pattern file and create panels from it as one undo step. AAMA files (ASTM D6673 layers) give panels with name, outline (curve points on layer 3 become smooth Bezier handles), notches (layers 4, 80 to 83), grain line (7), internal lines (8, role reference) and, when a sew line (14) lies inside the cut line (1), the sew line as outline with the gap as seam allowance. Plain DXF gives a panel per closed outline from lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines and inserted blocks, with open lines inside it as internal lines. Reports what was skipped.

fit_tolerance.description: Largest distance in mm between a point of the file and the Bezier curve fitted through the curve points.

flavour.description: aama reads one pattern piece per block with the ASTM D6673 layer numbers (1 cut line, 2 turn points, 3 curve points, 4 notches, 7 grain line, 8 internal lines, 14 sew line). plain reads closed outlines from lines, polylines, arcs, circles, splines and inserted blocks. auto picks aama when the file carries Piece Name or Style Name text.

mode.description: add appends the pieces to the pattern to the right of what is there. as_new replaces all panels of the pattern with the imported ones. Either is one undo step.

path.description: Path of the DXF file to read. ASCII DXF, release 12 or later.

smooth_facets.description: Plain files only. Treat runs of short polyline edges that turn by less than 15 degrees at each vertex as curves, so a curve that another program flattened comes back as a few Bezier segments instead of many corners.

units.description: Unit of the numbers in the file. Omit to detect it: AAMA files declare Units METRIC or ENGLISH, other files may carry the header variable INSUNITS, and millimetres is the fallback.

use_sew_line.description: When a piece has a closed sew line (layer 14) inside its cut line (layer 1), make the sew line the panel outline and turn the gap into the seam allowance.

commands.description: Write panels to an ASCII DXF file (release 12 entities). flavour.description: aama writes one block per piece with the ASTM D6673 layer numbers and system text. plain writes one drawing in the layout positions on named layers CUT, SEW, NOTCH, GRAIN, INTERNAL and NAME.

internal_labels.description: Write the annotation text with the piece name (layer 15) and the role labels of internal lines.

seam_allowance.description: Write the panel outline plus its seam allowance as the cut line (layer 1) and the outline itself as the sew line (layer 14). When off, or when a panel has no allowance, the outline is the cut line.

tolerance.description: Largest distance in mm between a curve and the polyline written for it.

commands.description: Move the draped garment from body A to body B without opening a seam. commands.description: Propose seams for the garment from the notches on the panels' own outline segments. Every open outline segment with notches is a candidate; segments pair only when their notch counts are equal, and all pairs are chosen together as one minimum-cost assignment where the cost is the relative length difference plus the mean difference of the notch positions (segments given the same tag in this call pair at zero cost). When both panels are placed in 3D, a small term for the distance between the segment midpoints settles ties between otherwise equal candidates; panels placed by hand or not placed work the same. Panels are never resized: a length mismatch is reported and left to the seam ratio. Works on panels placed by hand or not placed at all. Returns the proposals and the open segments; with apply the seams are created as one undo step and can be edited like any other seam.

points.description: length: two or more points of a polyline; distance: two points; circumference: three points that define the slice plane (instead of height).

items.description: A surface point: {panel, triangle, w: [w0, w1, w2]} barycentric on a mesh triangle, {panel, point: [x, y]} in panel space, or {position: [x, y, z]} in world mm.

data.description: The file bytes, base64 encoded (a data: URL prefix is accepted).

path.description: Absolute output path whose extension matches kind.

commands.label: Write Capture
commands.name: capture_write

commands.description: Start the Live Link for Unreal through USD: write the current draped garment as a usda layer into a folder at once, then replace it atomically every N simulation frames while the simulation runs (and after an edit, and when the simulation settles). Unreal's USD Stage reloads the layer when the file changes. The link follows the live positions without touching the document or undo; any file command (new, open) stops it. Starting again replaces the running link.

axis.description: Up axis stored in the layer. Unreal converts from the stage's upAxis.

every_frames.description: Write a new layer every this many simulation frames. Edits to the garment write at once, and a stopped simulation writes its last frame after a quarter second.

file.description: File name without extension; the layer is [folder]/[file].usda.

folder.description: Absolute folder the layer is written into; created when missing. Point Unreal's USD Stage at the file inside it.

format.description: Layer format. Only usd (usda text) is written.

thickness.description: Write the back face and side strips set by thickness.set.

commands.label: Start Live Link
commands.name: link_start

commands.description: Stop the Live Link. The last layer stays in the folder.
commands.label: Stop Live Link
commands.name: link_stop

commands.description: Read whether the Live Link is running, the folder and layer path, the write interval, how many layers were written, the frame of the last one, its size, the last error and why it stopped.

commands.name: link_state

commands.description: Store the whole garment state as a snapshot inside the project (entry snapshot/ID.json, plus snapshot/ID.png when a thumbnail is given as base64 PNG, at most 1 MiB). Does not change the garment, so it is not an undo step. At most 64 snapshots per project.

name.description: Snapshot name. Defaults to Snapshot N.

thumbnail.description: Optional PNG of the 3D window as base64 (a data URL is accepted), at most 1 MiB decoded.

commands.label: Save Snapshot
commands.name: snapshot_save

commands.description: List the snapshots stored in the project: id, name, created (unix seconds), panels, bytes and whether a thumbnail exists. With thumbnails true each item carries thumbnail_png (base64).

thumbnails.description: Include each thumbnail as base64 PNG in thumbnail_png.

commands.label: Snapshots
commands.name: snapshot_list

commands.description: Replace the garment with a snapshot's state. One undo step; bodies, the history and the other snapshots are kept.
commands.label: Restore Snapshot
commands.name: snapshot_restore

commands.description: Delete a snapshot and its thumbnail from the project. Not an undo step.
commands.label: Remove Snapshot
commands.name: snapshot_remove

commands.description: List the user library: fabrics (.ffab), trim and style files (.ffstyle), components (.ffcomp), garments (.ffbrc), poses (.ffpose) and motions (.ffmotion) from every configured library folder, with name, tags, thumbnail path and size. Files placed in the kind folders by hand are listed too.

kind.description: Only this kind. Leave out for all.

query.description: Case-insensitive text that must appear in the name or a tag.

commands.label: Library
commands.name: library_list

commands.description: Save a fabric, trim style, style, component, pose, motion or the open garment into the first library folder, with tags and an optional PNG thumbnail. Files are written atomically; the item can be inserted again with library.insert.

from.description: What to save: a fabric id, a trim or style id (style.list), a component id (component.list), a body id for a pose (default the first body) or a motion id. Leave out for kind garment, which saves the open project.

name.description: Item name.

thumbnail.description: Optional PNG as base64, at most 1 MiB.

commands.label: Add to Library
commands.name: library_add

commands.description: Bring a library fabric, trim, style, component, pose or motion into the open project. One undo step. A garment is not inserted: the error names the path for file.open.

body.description: Pose and motion only: the body to apply it to. Defaults to the first body.

joins.description: Component only: joins for component.insert, each {port, to: {component, port}, reversed, ease}.

commands.label: Insert from Library
commands.name: library_insert

commands.description: Delete a library item, its thumbnail and index entry from disk. Only files inside the library folders can be removed. Cannot be undone.

id.description: Library item id from library.list, for example fabric/denim.

commands.label: Remove from Library
commands.name: library_remove

commands.description: The folders the library reads and writes: the configured list, or the default [data dir]/library.
commands.label: Library Folders
commands.name: library_roots

commands.description: Set the library folders (absolute paths, created when missing, at most 8). The first receives new items. The list is stored in [data dir]/library_roots.json. An empty list returns to the default folder.

paths.description: Absolute folders. The first one receives new items. An empty list returns to the default [data dir]/library.

commands.label: Set Library Folders
commands.name: library_set_roots

commands.description: Group panels into a component: the author lists the panels, and names ports as edge spans of those panels with a length tolerance in mm. A component owns its own panels and their real seams; a panel belongs to at most one component. Nothing is inferred from panel shape.

name.description: Component name, for example Sleeve L.

panels.description: Panel ids the author groups into the component. A panel belongs to at most one component.

ports.description: Named edge spans of the component's own panels: [{name, spans: [{panel, segment, t0, t1}], tolerance}]. tolerance is a length in mm (default 5); t0 and t1 default to the whole segment.

commands.label: New Component
commands.name: component_create

commands.description: List components with their panels, ports (live length against the stored length, tolerance, whether the edge still exists, the join it is in) and internal seams, and the joins with the real seams they made.
commands.label: Components
commands.name: component_list

commands.description: Write a component to the library as a .ffcomp file: its panels, their internal seams and its ports, nothing else (no fabrics, trims or body). Path must be inside the component folder of a library folder; leave it out to use the first library folder.

name.description: Library name. Defaults to the component name.

path.description: Absolute .ffcomp path inside the component folder of a library folder. Leave out to save into the first library folder under the component's name.

thumbnail.description: Optional PNG as base64, at most 1 MiB.

commands.label: Save Component to Library
commands.name: component_save

commands.description: Insert a library component: its panels get new ids and are placed beside the garment, its internal seams and ports are recreated, and the given joins become ordinary seams between real panel edges. One undo step.

from.description: Library component id (component/sleeve-l) or an absolute .ffcomp path inside a library folder.

joins.description: Joins to make now: [{port, to: {component, port}, reversed, ease}], where port is a port of the inserted component and to a port of a component in the project.

commands.label: Insert Component
commands.name: component_insert

commands.description: Replace a component with a library component: remove the old panels, insert the new ones centred where the old were, and recreate every join by port name. Refused when a joined port name is missing or its length differs by more than the tolerance (unless ease is true, which sews with a seam ratio). Panels are never graded or resized. One undo step.

ease.description: Accept ports whose length differs by more than the tolerance and sew them with a seam ratio. A missing port name always refuses the swap. Panels are never resized.

with.description: Library component id or an absolute .ffcomp path inside a library folder.

commands.label: Swap Component
commands.name: component_swap

commands.description: Join a port of one component to a port of another: one seam per pair of spans (or one multi-span seam when the span counts differ) between the real panel edges, recorded as a join. Refused when the port lengths differ by more than the tolerance unless ease is true.

ease.description: Allow ports whose lengths differ by more than the tolerance; the seam gets ratio = b length / a length.

reversed.description: Pair the start of side a with the end of side b (right for two counter-clockwise outlines meeting along an edge).

commands.label: Join Components
commands.name: component_join

commands.description: Compare a library component with a project component by port names and lengths only: for every joined port of the project component, whether the other has a port of that name and its length is within the tolerance. Changes nothing.

id.description: Project component that would be replaced.

with.description: Library component id or an absolute .ffcomp path inside a library folder.

commands.label: Check Component Swap
commands.name: component_check

commands.description: Remove a component and its joins. The panels and seams stay unless delete_panels is true.

delete_panels.description: Also delete the component's panels and the seams on them. Without it only the grouping and its joins are removed and the panels and seams stay.

commands.label: Remove Component
commands.name: component_remove

commands.description: Build the sample modular T-shirt: tshirt groups the drafted sample into components and joins; sleeveless adds a no-sleeve armhole binding component for swapping.

like.description: sleeveless only: the component whose port sets the binding lengths (a sleeve).

name.description: tshirt groups the drafted sample T-shirt (sample.load tshirt) into Torso, Sleeve L and Sleeve R with an armhole port and a join each. sleeveless adds a no-sleeve variant: two armhole binding strips as one component with an armhole port the lengths of another component's port.

port.description: sleeveless only: the port name to match.
